exposure: Cigarette smoke (one or two cigarettes per day)
outcome: Serum levels of soluble FMS-like tyrosine kinase-1 (sFlt-1)
Serum levels of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)
cohort: The participants were pregnant mice exposed to cigarette smoke.
finding: Exposure to two cigarettes per day significantly decreased serum sFlt-1 levels compared to no exposure, a decrease that was reversed by an AhR antagonist and mimicked by an AhR agonist, suggesting a role for AhR in regulating sFlt-1.
